content: Rickets is a condition characterized by the softening and weakening of bones in children, which can lead to fractures and skeletal deformities. It is one of the most common childhood diseases in many developing countries. The primary cause of rickets is a deficiency in vitamin D, although insufficient dietary calcium can also contribute to the development of the condition. While rickets can occur in adults, it is predominantly observed in children who experience severe malnutrition, often as a result of famine or starvation during the early stages of childhood. In adults, a similar condition is referred to as osteomalacia, which is also typically caused by a deficiency in vitamin D. The etymology of the word rickets remains uncertain. However, the term rachitis, derived from the Greek word meaning inflammation of the spine, was later adopted as the scientific term for rickets, primarily due to the phonetic similarity between the two words.
